UNIT ex_dealer_mono. Passage: Example 5.5 "Monotonicity at arbitrary epsilon" (lines 2216-2250);
abstract "its law interaction is monotone at every interaction strength"; Rem 5.7.

Faithful statement:
- Setting: n=m=d=1, G=1, any sigma-finite nu (standing basis), sigma_c in R, h_c in L^2(nu),
  beta1,beta2>0, any epsilon >= 0.
- Coefficients: b=-beta1 y, sigma=sigma_c-beta1 z, h=h_c-beta1 u-eps A_{mu^U}(u), f=beta2 x,
  g(x,rho)=x, where A_lambda(u) = int grad V(u-v) lambda(dv) (Bochner integral in L^2(nu)),
  grad V(w)=w/sqrt(1+||w||^2), mu^U the U-marginal of the measure argument.
- Conclusion: for EVERY eps >= 0, Assumption 2.5 holds with alpha=1, beta1, beta2 (the constants of
  Ex 5.1(i)), no smallness/margin: terminal E<dX_T,dX_T> >= E|dX_T|^2 for all X_T,X'_T in L^2(F_T),
  and interior (2.7) for a.e. (here every) t and all diagonal pairs. In particular the key step
  E<A_{mu^U}(U)-A_{mu'^U}(U'), U-U'>_{L^2(nu)} >= 0 along diagonal pairs, so
  E int <dh,dU> nu <= -beta1 E||dU||^2. Constants constraints alpha+beta1>0 etc. hold.
- Quantifier: eps universally quantified, no restriction beyond eps>=0; the constants alpha=1,
  beta1, beta2 must not depend on eps.

Standing setting (paper §2), shared by every proposition below: a filtered probability space
satisfying the usual conditions, horizon T>0, dimensions n,m,d>=1, a d-dim Brownian motion W and an
independent Poisson random measure N on R_+ x E with intensity dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a
countably generated (E,E) (so L^2(nu;R^j) separable); the filtration is the usual augmentation of
the one generated by W, N and an independent F_0. H = R^n x R^m x R^{m x d} x L^2(nu;R^m) with the
HILBERT (l^2-sum) norm |x|^2+|y|^2+|z|_F^2+||u||^2 (not a sup norm); W_2 on P_2(H) w.r.t. that norm.
Coefficients b,sigma,f: [0,T] x H x P_2(H) -> R^n, R^{n x d}, R^m; h: [0,T] x H x P_2(H) -> L^2(nu;R^n);
g: R^n x P_2(R^n) -> R^m; deterministic, jointly Borel; h Borel into L^2(nu;R^n) (2.3).
Diagonal input at t: (Theta, Law Theta) with Theta in L^2(Omega,F_t;H).
Ass 2.2: xi_0 in L^2(F_0), origin values b(.,0,delta_0), sigma(.,0,delta_0), h(.,0,.,delta_0),
 f(.,0,delta_0) in L^2(0,T).
Ass 2.3: exists L>=0: for a.e. t, all diagonal pairs, |db|+|dsigma|_F+||dh||+|df| <= L(|dX|+|dY|+|dZ|_F
 +||dU||+W_2(mu,mu')) a.s.; and for all X_T,X'_T in L^2(F_T), |dg_T|<=L(|dX_T|+W_2(rho,rho')) a.s.
Ass 2.4: G in R^{m x n} full rank; ||G|| operator norm; c_G = s_min(G)^{-2}.
Ass 2.5: terminal E<dg_T, G dX_T> >= alpha E|G dX_T|^2 for all X_T,X'_T in L^2(F_T); interior (2.7)
 for a.e. t and all diagonal pairs, with alpha,beta1,beta2>=0, alpha+beta1>0, beta1+beta2>0,
 beta1>0 if m<n, alpha,beta2>0 if m>n.
(2.12) weighted margin, (2.13) unweighted margin (m=n): extra -c E[...] on the right of (2.7).
Solution: Theta=(X,Y,Z,U) in S := S^2 x S^2 x H^2_W x H^2_N (cadlag adapted X,Y; predictable Z, U
 L^2(nu)-valued), both identities of (1.1) a.s. for every t, h at the predictable tuple
 (Theta_t^-, mu_t^-), mu, mu^- the Borel law flows of Lemma A.1. Weak class H^2 (L^2(0,T) cadlag
 adapted X,Y). Equality: X,Y indistinguishable, Z dt x dP-a.e., U dt x dP x nu-a.e.

comparison.text:
ex_dealer_mono vs my reading.
- Setting as ex_dealer (n = m = d = 1, any sigma-finite nu, beta1, beta2 > 0, sigma_c, h_c,
  every eps >= 0). OK.
- Conclusions: (a) for every t and all diagonal pairs, E<A_{mu^U}(U) - A_{mu'^U}(U'), U - U'>_{L^2(nu)}
  >= 0 (inner on Lp 2 = the L^2(nu) inner product, mu^U = margU of p.2 = Law U); (b) for every t,
  E int <dh(e), dU(e)> nu(de) <= -beta1 E||dU||^2; (c) Assumption25 with G = 1, alpha = 1, beta1,
  beta2 (terminal, interior for a.e. t, admissible constants). The constants do not depend on eps.
  These are the printed claims ("monotone at every interaction strength", "(2.7) holds with the
  constants alpha = 1, beta1, beta2 for every eps >= 0, no smallness, no margin"). Statements (a)-(b)
  are made at every t (stronger than a.e.). OK.
- Witness ex_dealer_hypotheses: infinite-activity dealer marks. OK.
Verdict: faithful.
